questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The children is crying loudly because they have lost all their favorite toys.
questions.explanation: The error lies in 'is crying loudly'. 'Children' is a plural noun, so it must take a plural verb. The correct phrase should be 'The children are crying loudly' to maintain proper subject-verb agreement.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Neither of the two boys have brought their respective mathematics textbooks to the class.
questions.explanation: The error is in the segment 'have brought their'. The pronoun 'Neither' acts as a singular subject and must be followed by a singular verb and singular possessive pronoun. It should be corrected to 'has brought his'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Hardly had I reached the railway station than the express train departed from the platform.
questions.explanation: The error lies in the use of 'than'. The adverb 'hardly' is always paired with the conjunction 'when', not 'than'. ('No sooner' is paired with 'than'). The correct sentence is 'Hardly had I reached the railway station when the express train departed...'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Unless you do not work hard, you will definitely fail the upcoming board examination.
questions.explanation: The error is 'do not work hard'. The word 'unless' inherently carries a negative meaning ('if not'). Using 'not' along with 'unless' in the same clause creates a double negative. It should correctly be 'Unless you work hard...'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

One of my best friend is going to travel to the United States next month.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'One of' must always be followed by a plural noun, because you are selecting one from a group of many. The singular verb 'is' correctly matches 'One', but 'friend' must be pluralized. It should be 'One of my best friends'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The inquiry committee were divided in its opinion regarding the final verdict of the case.
questions.explanation: When a collective noun like 'committee' is divided in opinion, it is treated as plural (hence 'were divided' is correct). However, the pronoun must also match the plural nature. 'its opinion' should be corrected to 'their opinions'.

questions.stem:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Despite lacking formal education, he is clearly more smarter than his younger brother.
questions.explanation: The error lies in the phrase 'more smarter'. The word 'smarter' is already the comparative degree of 'smart'. Adding 'more' creates an incorrect double comparative. It should simply be 'smarter than'.
